name: Skiathos
title: Holidays in Skiathos
intro: A pine-covered island with over 60 sandy beaches, a lively harbour town and the dramatic runway that planespotters love. Here's what Skiathos is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Skiathos town's white houses above the harbour and yachts
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June and September are best for warm sea and calmer beaches. July and August are busy and hot. The season runs from May to October.

things.name: Koukounaries
things.blurb: A long golden beach backed by pine forest and a lagoon.

things.name: Lalaria
things.blurb: White pebbles and a rock arch, reached only by boat.

things.name: Banana beach
things.blurb: A lively sandy cove with clear water.

things.name: Skiathos town
things.blurb: Lanes, churches and harbour bars, plus the Bourtzi headland.

things.name: Skopelos
things.blurb: The Mamma Mia! island, a short ferry away.

things.name: Plane-watching
things.blurb: See jets land just over the road at the end of the runway.

faqs.question: Is Skiathos worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It has some of Greece's best sandy beaches, a lively town and easy island-hopping to Skopelos.

faqs.question: How do you get to Skiathos?
faqs.answer: Fly into Skiathos, which has direct summer flights from the UK. The town is a few minutes from the airport.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Skiathos?
Is Skiathos good for families?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many beaches are sandy and shallow, and buses run along the south coast.

faqs.question: Can you visit Skopelos from Skiathos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ferries take about 45 minutes, and boat trips visit the Mamma Mia! chapel.
